mathematical_review: Independent reconstruction and original-object/hypothesis checking; not a Lean replay.

findings.detail: The integral Hilbert-90 parameter and factorial sequence have the stated archimedean and finite limits. At nonsplit primes the parameter and its inverse are units; finitely many projector denominators are cleared. Removing finitely supported split factors leaves every tail element in one fixed compact lattice stabilizer. Product-topology convergence inside that fixed compact group justifies the full-adelic limit and kills the infinite part of every rational reflection.

The two-reflection argument works for every nondegenerate Hermitian form, including indefinite forms and rank zero. The Cayley-chart weak approximation proof avoids finitely many forbidden rational norm-one scalars. Reflection-parameter corrections preserve the desired finite-place precision and make all other nonsplit components integral. The exact factorization g=gamma_f^{-1} s k, followed by factorial congruences, kills the finite part. This explicitly extends QD13--QD14 beyond their former definite-only scope.

The relative operator preserves the same theta space, commutes with its Heisenberg operators, and preserves its original Haar norm, so the previously reconstructed CW15 applies. A nonzero vector makes the scalar unique; evaluation with nonzero denominator proves continuity. Group laws and rational evaluation at zero prove the character and rational-triviality statements. The zero theta-space case is separately harmless.

CW3 produces a nonzero fixed vector on the original standard self-dual finite Hom lattice without a new Weil action. The corrected and raw Heisenberg operators agree on each isotropic split half. WA5 then yields an algebraic functional invariant on every theta vector. The same separation/telescoping argument applies to the difference vector in BTH15. Positive split scalars and the unit-modulus character give exact equality, not equality up to an unknown scalar.

CW23 and WA18 construct a full datum on the same functions and with the same final splitting characters; BTH14 identifies it with the originally supplied datum. For a nonsplit norm-one determinant, the host residue involution gives an integral unit x=b+a*bar(b) satisfying a=x/bar(x). All original and eta characters kill this unit. Dyadic places are split, so division by two upgrades the original IsLatVac law to the local raw fixing required by FixesVacAt. No unproved preservation of canonical vacuum normalization under arbitrary twists is used.

The original frames and their inverses give the same completed Hom-lattice stabilizers. Selected split places give the crossed determinant factor; unselected split places and nonsplit places give one. Finite-support truncations converge within one fixed compact product, so pointwise om_cont and character continuity give the exact original global stabilizer identity.

These are category B implication proofs on supplied original data. They close the potential additional finite-covariance input on the stated base-theta route. They do not construct the common selector, original reading, smooth cuspidal extension, simultaneous rational tests, or RowsHold0_3. Equality is asserted only on the original theta space, not arbitrary ambient extensions.
